verdict.rationale: Mercury Books explicitly ties bank accounts into continuous, automatic reconciliation and categorization ('Accounts reconcile in real time... without manual work'), which covers the core ledger-vs-bank matching for accountants. However, the evidence never describes a review surface that explicitly separates matched vs unmatched vs duplicate transactions for bank reconciliation—duplicate detection is only documented for bill pay, not bank transactions, and Mercury's own honest-scope post admits automation can't make all decisions, implying manual review is still needed but doesn't describe how flagged discrepancies are surfaced. missing for 10: explicit unmatched-transaction queue, explicit duplicate-transaction detection for bank reconciliation (not just bills), and independent/hands-on confirmation of the reconciliation review UI.
